intended_object: The ℤ-lattice U_ℤ · ℤ^{GeckIndex} inside the Geck module ℚ^{GeckIndex}: the ℤ-span of all vectors ρ(u)e_x, where u runs over the simple-generator Kostant ℤ-form U_ℤ of U(L), ρ is the defining matrix representation of Geck's split Lie algebra L, and e_x are the standard coordinate vectors. It is a stable, admissible lattice as in Humphreys §27. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body is `Subring.orbitOfRep (t.kostantForm ht) (t.geckRepresentation ht) (range fun x => Pi.single x 1)`. `orbitOfRep S ρ X` is defined as `Submodule.span ℤ {v | ∃ a ∈ S, ∃ x ∈ X, ρ a x = v}`. Here S is the pinned Kostant form, i.e. the subring generated by the divided powers e_i^n/n! and f_i^n/n! and by the binomials (h_i choose n). ρ is the matrix representation of U(L) on GeckIndex → ℚ, and X is the set of standard basis vectors.

So the definition is exactly the ℤ-span of the U_ℤ-translates of the standard coordinate vectors, which is what the docstring says. Because 1 ∈ S, the set includes the standard lattice ℤ^n. It is stable under S because S is closed under multiplication. Since U_ℤ contains 1, the module U_ℤ·ℤ^n is the same thing as this span.

This is a specific object attached to a specific construction, Geck's realisation of the split Lie algebra of a Dynkin type. The general construction already exists in the library as `Subring.orbitOfRep`, at the level of an arbitrary subring, algebra representation and generating set, and this definition only specialises it. So it is not too narrow. Mathlib has no counterpart for Kostant forms or admissible lattices.
